speech: Everyone told me dust mites are just something you have to live with. Wash, vacuum, repeat, forever. They were wrong.
Let me ask you something. Actually, let me ask you three things. Okay, first, what would you do if you found a snake in your house?
You call somebody to catch it and get it out of there, right?
I mean, you wouldn't just say, well, I guess I live with a snake now. Of course not. You get rid of it.
Okay, second question. What if you found bugs crawling around in your bed? What would you do?
You'd spray them, you'd kill them, you'd clean everything up and get them out of your bed.
What do you do when you find out there are dust mites living in your bed?
Well, you capture them and get rid of them too, right? Oh wait, you can't because you can't even see them.
So what are you supposed to do? Well, that's the problem. You basically just accept it. You say,
okay, I guess dust mites live in my bed now. And instead of getting rid of them,
you just try to make living with them a little easier. You wash your sheets in hot water,
you vacuum more often, you run an air purifier, you take antihistamines, maybe you buy a special
mattress cover. And listen, maybe some of that helps. But you're still basically saying,
you guys can stay in my bed. I'll just keep dealing with everything around you. Because
really, what other choice do you have? You can't see them. You can't catch them. So you just
learn to live with them. Well, what if I told you that's not true? What if you could capture dust
mites? What if you could trap them, pick them up and throw them away, just like you would with any
other pest? Well, now you can. Visa called capture kites and the way they work, it's actually pretty
covet. Scientists discovered that dust mites use chemical signals called pheromones to find one
another. One of those signals is called narrow propionate. To a dust mite, that signal basically
says, hey, other dust mites are over here. Capture cards use that signal as a lure. So instead of
sitting there and hoping a dust mite accidentally walks onto the card, the card draws them toward
it. The mites follow the signal. They move toward the part and once they're inside, an adhesive
layer traps them so they can't call back out. You just place the cards near your mattress and pillows
as directed and let them work. No sprays, no insecticides, nothing to plug in. Then, when
it's time to replace the card, you pick it up and throw it away. Mites and all. That's it.
So now, you don't want to treat dust mites like invisible roommates you're stuck with. You may not
be able to see them, but now you can capture them. You can remove them. And you can finally do more
than just clean around them and hope for the best. Tap below to see how capture cards work.
